data.exact_reserve_text: During 2015, we have been able to release prior year reserves of $40.3m (2014: $33.9m).

named_events.loss_description: settled our policyholders' claims within a month

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate released $40.3 million in prior year reserves in 2015, representing a 5.71% release relative to opening gross claims outstanding. This favorable development was primarily driven by a benign claims environment, lower-than-expected natural catastrophe activity, and easing claims activity in the US economy, particularly on professional liability and management liability books. The syndicate's consistent reserving philosophy, which includes setting initial reserves with risk margins, also contributed to these releases as uncertainties reduced over time.
raw_causal_phrases: driven largely by an increase in the amount released from prior year reserves.
Overall, the claims environment has been favourable during 2015, when we have again experienced lower than expected natural catastrophe activity.
The economy in our principal market, the US, continues to rebound from the economic downturn, easing claims activity on the professional liability and management liability books.
These positive trends in the US, and the relatively benign natural catastrophe claims environment, have contributed to strong reserve releases and an improved claims ratio of 45% (2014: 48%).
Beazley has a consistent reserving philosophy, with initial reserves being set to include risk margins that may be released over time as and when any uncertainty reduces.
We therefore frequently have an opportunity to release prior year reserves into our earnings as claims crystallise.
